sections.title: Form and cultivation
sections.text: A perennial terrestrial bromeliad forming a rosette, usually 1–2 m tall and wide; its rigid leaves can reach 1 m. The dense inflorescence bears many purple flowers. Their fruits fuse with the axis into a fleshy syncarp crowned by leaves and reaching about 30 cm. This South American domesticated cultigen is now grown throughout the tropics; its exact origin and wild ancestors remain uncertain.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The ripe fruit is eaten. Kew notes that unripe fruit may irritate the throat and act as a purgative. Leaf margins vary among cultivars, from spiny to nearly smooth.
